newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends quiet session firmer.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends quiet session firmer.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures ended modestly higher on Monday, but turnover was thin, with the London market still closed for the Easter holiday, trading sources said.
Cocoa prices rose from the outset, peaking at $1,460 a tonne basis the spot May contract on speculative buying, but scale-up trade selling emerged toward the highs and sparked a modest retracement.
"It was very, very quiet," one trader said. "We got up to $1,460 early, but there was no follow-through and we ended up sitting in mid-range for most of the day."
Most-active May ended up $3 a tonne, at $1,453, traded from $1,460 to $1,445. Second-month July also rose $3, to $1,482, while the outer months closed $8 to $10 higher.
Technically, traders said the May contract would need to clear Wednesday's close of $1,461 to solidify its stance. Further resistance was seen at $1,475. Support was pegged near $1,425.

Dealers said the latest CFTC Commitment of Traders data, which showed an increase of net long position (non-commercial plus non-reportable) to 24,763 lots as of March 25, was within expectations and largely priced into the market.
Volume on the exchange was estimated at 5,208 lots, with AAs (against actuals) accounting for nearly 2,000 lots, traders said.
